problems.code_says: Three test scripts set the variable, not one. `bin/ci/test-generated-output-staging.sh` sets it two times and `bin/ci/test-remove-whitespace.sh` sets it one time. These two scripts are the only ones that source `bin/ci/test/darwin-file-commands.sh`, so they are the only setters for the fake `chmod` that this file writes. `bin/ci/test-shared-nfs.sh` does not source that file. It sets the variable only for the fake `chmod` that it writes itself. The cell therefore names 1 of 3 setter files (1 of 4 set sites), and it gives no setter for the first reader that the row lists.

`coverage-combine` reads two inputs. It searches the Cabal coverage build directory for the test coverage file `ingest-tests.tix`, and it reads `build-all-combined.tix` at the fixed path `$(BUILD_ALL_TIX_DIR)`. The true part of the sentence is that the target never reads `COVERAGE_TIX_DIR`, so it does not see a `build-all.sh` result in another directory. As written, the sentence says the target has one input file.
problems.corrected_cell: In coverage mode `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) creates the directory. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` to `<directory>/<model>.tix` for each model. At the end it combines all `.tix` files (Haskell coverage counts) of the directory into `build-all-combined.tix`. Used only when `COVERAGE` is not empty. `.tix` files of an earlier run are combined too. `make build-all-coverage` sets the default directory itself and deletes the `.tix` files there first. `make coverage-combine` does not read `COVERAGE_TIX_DIR`. It looks for the `build-all.sh` result only at `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix/build-all-combined.tix`. It also reads the test coverage file `ingest-tests.tix`. The working directory of the script must be `ingest/`.

notes: Result for this sample of 10 rows: 8 correct, 2 imprecise, 0 wrong. Both imprecise rows have one problem each, and each problem is an incomplete list of files, not a wrong value or a wrong effect. Method: for each variable I ran git grep on the name, read every read site and every set site, and followed the helpers and callers. I ran no build, no test and no repository script, and I changed no file in the checkout. One fact comes from outside the repository: the command nproc (GNU coreutils 8.32 on this host) returned 2 with OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2 and 6 with OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=999 on a shell with 6 CPUs, so the variable lowers the result and never raises it. Details that I saw and did not grade, because they do not change what a reader would do: (1) TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR: the final book can be larger than TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS when one append needs more pages than the cap, and the DMA allocation limit also bounds it (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:999 and :1071). The row sentence is about the growth result, and the cap does apply to that. (2) TRON_AMX_DISABLE: for an EAGLE draft model the FUSE file is under attention_eagle/, not attention/ (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:919). (3) TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES: a SIGUSR1 capture also goes to traced when TRACE_FILE has the value traced (src/pos/perf.cpp:162). (4) COVERAGE_TIX_DIR: an empty value counts as unset (ingest/build-all.sh:47). (5) TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE: the abort for a bad value happens when the shared thread pool is first created, not at the first line of startup (h/tron/threading.hpp:755). (6) REAL_CHMOD: the Read by cell is right, but it would be clearer if it said which test uses which fake chmod.
